headline: Historic Town Stays and National Forest Access
reservation: Dahlonega requires no town entry permit, but Amicalola Falls State Park requires a daily parking pass. Lodging in the historic square for festivals like Gold Rush Days or Christmas must be secured months in advance via official local providers.

days.title: Gold Rush History and Town Square

stops.name: Dahlonega Gold Museum
stops.detail: Explore the 1836 courthouse to learn about the nation's first major gold rush.

stops.name: Consolidated Gold Mine
stops.detail: Descend into underground tunnels to see how quartz veins were mined historically.

days.driving: Local walking and short 5-minute drives; parking can be tight on the square.
days.note: Underground tours maintain a constant cool temperature; a light jacket is suggested.

days.title: Appalachian Trails and Waterfalls

stops.name: Amicalola Falls State Park
stops.detail: View the tallest cascading waterfall in Georgia via a series of stairs and trails.

stops.name: Springer Mountain
stops.detail: Visit the southern terminus of the Appalachian Trail; high-clearance vehicles are advised for the forest road.

days.driving: Allow 45–60 minutes for mountain roads; conditions vary with rainfall.
days.note: Amicalola Falls requires a Georgia State Parks pass, available at the gate.

days.title: Rivers and Blue Ridge Vistas
days.start: Suggested: 9:30 AM from North Georgia Hills

stops.name: Chestatee River
stops.detail: Enjoy seasonal tubing or kayaking; check water levels and outfitter schedules.

stops.name: Woody Gap
stops.detail: Stop for panoramic views and a short hike to Preachers Rock on the Appalachian Trail.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for mountain transit; expect winding roads.
days.note: River activities are highly seasonal and dependent on recent rainfall and temperature.

intel.title: Downtown Square Limitations
intel.text: Weekend parking in the historic square is heavily contested. Utilize the peripheral public lots near the university for easier access during festivals.

intel.title: Mountain Topography Effects
intel.text: Expect total signal loss at Woody Gap and Springer Mountain trailheads. Download topo maps for the Chattahoochee-Oconee National Forest before leaving town.

intel.title: Last Fuel Points
intel.text: Fill your tank in Dahlonega before heading north into the national forest. Gas stations are absent along the forest service roads leading to trailheads.

intel.title: Festival Congestion
intel.text: Gold Rush Days in October attract massive crowds; plan for significant walking distances and restaurant waits. Arrive by 8 AM for these events.

intel.title: Forest Road Maintenance
intel.text: The road to Springer Mountain is unpaved and can be rutted. Check official Forest Service alerts for closures following heavy mountain storms.

plan.arrival: Fly into Atlanta (ATL) or DeKalb Peachtree (PDK), then drive north via GA-400. Check into your inn before the evening square rush.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are fine for town, but a vehicle with moderate clearance is better for forest service roads like FS 42.
plan.goldenHour: Preachers Rock at Woody Gap offers a wide-angle view of the Blue Ridge foothills for sunset enthusiasts.
